requirements.text: A cumulative GPA of at least 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0 — or a score percentile of 80% or above on a 100-point scale, or a rank in the top 20% of the class

The Embassy of Japan in Nepal requires 70% marks (CGPA 3.1) for Natural Sciences and 60% marks (CGPA 2.5) for Humanities and Social Sciences, averaged across the +2 and above degree. This is a Nepal-specific bar set by the mission, not a MEXT-wide rule.
requirements.scope_note: Nepal-specific. The mission sets this bar; MEXT's own guidelines do not. A reader applying from another country must check their own mission.

of.text: CGPA of at least B/B+ on the US system, or a 2nd upper classification on the UK system

requirements.text: 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent) is the minimum permitted GPA. KAUST adds context for applicants: typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3, and 75% have a GPA above 3.5 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent).
requirements.not_a_requirement: The figures 3.3 and 3.5 describe who was typically admitted, not a threshold. They are recorded here as context and must never be compared against.

of.quote: No minimum GPA is stated in the Edital.
of.text: No minimum GPA is stated in the Edital. Academic admission requirements are set by the individual postgraduate programme the candidate applies to, and the Edital states that CAPES's requirements and the programme's requirements are cumulative.

of.applies_to: top 10% of graduates in the previous study programme

requirements.text: Students must have achieved excellent academic results in their previous study programme(s), which must be relevant to the Master's programme for which they are applying. As an indication, the student is amongst the top 10% of graduates in his/her previous study programme. Note that proof of ranking is not required – this information is purely to indicate the level of competitiveness.
requirements.not_a_requirement: TU Delft states the 10% figure “as an indication” and says proof of ranking is not required. It is a statement of the competitive level, not a gate the reader is asked to evidence.

of.quote: There is no formula for admission, and there are no scores, achievements, or stories that automatically qualify you for admission.
of.text: Knight-Hennessy publishes two baseline eligibility requirements — admission to a full-time Stanford graduate degree programme, and a first bachelor's degree earned in January 2020 or later — and no academic threshold. The admission page states there is no formula for admission and no score that automatically qualifies an applicant.

KTH names four scholarship selection criteria, the first of which is “the applicant's grades (GPA or equivalent)”, alongside the ranking of the university that awarded the bachelor's degree, relevant extracurricular research or work experience, and the applicant's motivation on sustainable development. No minimum grade, GPA or class threshold is published.
of.varies_by: no published threshold — grades are one of four weighted criteria

of.text: Stipend-bearing Graduate Research Scholarships are “offered to eligibile candidates ranked highest by relevant selection panels based on their academic results for prior study and their research potential in their field of study”. No minimum GPA, WAM or honours class is published; the only stated eligibility is having applied for, or being enrolled in, a graduate research degree.
of.varies_by: no published threshold — candidates are ranked against each other

of.text: Chevening's published eligibility requires an undergraduate degree “that qualifies you for a UK master's programme” and an unconditional offer from at least one of the three courses applied to. No degree classification, GPA or grade threshold is published by Chevening itself — the academic bar is set by the university making the offer, not by the scheme.
of.varies_by: the admitting university, not Chevening — no classification published by the scheme

requirements.not_a_requirement: A 2:1 (upper second-class) is widely repeated as a Chevening requirement in third-party guides. It does not appear in Chevening's own published eligibility criteria, which delegate the academic bar to the unconditional offer. It is recorded here as absent from the source, not as a threshold to meet.

of.text: SI publishes no academic threshold for the Scholarship for Global Professionals. The documents it requires are a CV, proof of work and leadership experience, two references, a passport copy and a motivation statement — no transcript or record of grades is requested. Admission, and with it the academic entry requirement, is handled by University Admissions rather than by SI.
of.varies_by: the admitting university via University Admissions — SI assesses no academic criterion

of.text: Admission is subject to the approval of the TERRA Managing Board and is based on the applicant's academic ability, motivation, recommendation letters and language proficiency. Applications will be assessed solely on academic merit, ability and potential. The academic evaluation of the candidate's curriculum is based on the following criteria: previous higher education studies; content and relevance of prior studies / quality of the awarding institution; relevant professional experience; recommendation letters; motivation letter; additional information (publications, awards, etc.). No GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class rank is published as a bar.

Applicants are expected to have a higher education degree with a minimum of: a Bachelor's degree with 240 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to 4 years of study), or Bachelor's and/or Master's degree(s) with 300 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to 5 years of study) — the 300-credit requirement is mandatory for all students whose mobility track includes UNIFI. Applicants must hold a degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture or equivalent qualifications.
requirements.varies_by: mobility track — 300 ECTS where the track includes UNIFI, 240 ECTS otherwise

of.text: Admission to NORISK will be decided on a competitive basis; the students are assessed on the basis of their previous academic record. Applications will be assessed solely on academic merit, ability and potential. The academic evaluation of the candidate's curriculum is based on the following criteria: previous higher education studies; content and relevance of prior studies / quality of the awarding institution; relevant professional experience; recommendation letters; motivation letter; additional information (publications, awards, etc.). No GPA, grade average, marks percentage or class rank is published as a bar.

Applicants must have completed at least 240 ECTS education in Civil Engineering, Industrial and/or Systems Engineering, Materials Engineering, Environmental Engineering or related fields, having been awarded a recognised degree in any of such fields. For students having a study period in UNIPD (either coursework or dissertation) a minimum of 300 ECTS education is required, including specified credits in hydraulics, structural mechanics, structural engineering and geotechnics.
requirements.varies_by: mobility track — 300 ECTS where the track includes UNIPD, 240 ECTS otherwise

Students are expected to have a higher education degree with a minimum of: Bachelor and/or Master degree(s) with 300 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to a graduation with a total of 5 years of studies) — this requirement becomes mandatory for all students whose mobility track includes UNINA — or Bachelor degree(s) with 240 ECTS-credit points (typically equivalent to a graduation with a total of 4 years of studies). The degree must be in Civil Engineering, Mechanical and/or Industrial Engineering, Materials Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Polymers Engineering or related fields.
requirements.varies_by: mobility track — 300 ECTS where the track includes UNINA, 240 ECTS otherwise

of.text: Ranking is performed on basis of the following criteria: academic level, University of last degree, English proficiency, motivation, reference letters. Within the eligible candidates selected, the consortium awards scholarships for mobility on basis of the score obtained in the selection ranking. No GPA, marks percentage, degree classification or numeric ranking threshold is published as a bar.

Students must have a Bachelor's Degree (180 ECTS) in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science or related disciplines: Geo-science, Nano-science, Materials engineering. (Bachelors in Mechanical engineering and in Mechatronics are not adapted to the Mamaself program.)

of.text: The minimum GPA (Grade Point Average) depends on the country of study, as defined by IHE Delft (based on a thorough comparative assessment done at a higher level in the Netherlands). In case of doubt, the programme coordinator is contacted. Following the eligibility check, a shortlist of around 50-80 applicants eligible for a scholarship is built by the coordinator of the programme in close collaboration with the student admission office, based on the relevance and grade of the obtained bachelor degree and followed disciplines, relevant work experience, other academic qualifications or activities, the number of applicants per country and the letter of motivation.
of.varies_by: country of study — the programme states that a minimum GPA exists and is set per country of study, but publishes no figure for any country

of.applies_to: the best 35% of students in the qualifying degree

requirements.text: The qualifying degree has to be passed with an average grade higher or equal to B (or a final grading higher or equal to B) according to the ECTS grading system, i.e. the best 35% of students (corresponding to a grade of up to 2.8 ("gut"/"good") in the German grading scale). The qualifying degree must be a first-cycle degree qualification according to the European Qualifications Framework or an equivalent degree qualification in the field of Civil Engineering, subject to an examination of equivalence by the programme's Admission Board.

of.text: This record is the European Commission's catalogue of the 218 Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes currently supported by the EU, not a programme itself, and it publishes no admission criteria. It directs applicants to "visit the program's official website and directly contact the consortium for information on courses, application procedures, and scholarship availability". The academic requirement belongs to each consortium's own programme, and ScholarHub records it there — TERRA, NORISK, FRP++, MaMaSELF+, MS² and Flood Risk Management each carry their own entry in this file.
